description: ClearWater Modules is a Python library of water-temperature, nutrient, general-constituent, contaminant and mercury process routines. The US Army Engineer Research and Development Center develops it to attach water-quality calculations to existing hydrodynamic and watershed models, not rebuilding their flow solvers. A host model provides a spatial domain, flow fields, boundary conditions, constituent concentrations and simulation dates; outputs are calculated water-quality changes for that domain. The README lists HEC-RAS-2D, GSSHA and CE-QUAL-W2 as intended hosts, while temperature and nutrient modules have specifically been coupled through ClearWater-riverine. Spatial and temporal resolution follow the selected host model. MIT source, examples and documentation are freely available. A limitation is that listed potential host tools are not evidence that all process modules are integrated and validated with each one. Local reaction parameters and observations remain necessary for credible water-quality claims. The library supports reservoir and river treatment or contaminant scenarios. The catalogue's data-freshwater-watch-citizen-science-water-quality is a separate observation source that might help local evaluation, but no pairing was tested. No model or dataset was downloaded.
